item: dayz-rag MCP server (server.py, voyage_common.py, README, tests)
reason: Mostly solid. The 75 MCP tests pass (py -m pytest -q .claude/mcp/dayz-rag). In the full requested suite, 3 of 4528 tests fail, all outside this server. All three tools carry readOnlyHint, and openWorldHint is set correctly: true for the search tool, false for the two local tools. Tool descriptions are clear. Errors raise and reach the client with isError=true, and a test runs this through the MCP layer. Retries, the cache, rebuild detection, the drive guard and worker-thread offload are all tested. The README matches the code. One concrete defect confirmed on P:: get_dayz_file only applies its 200 KB limit when neither line_start nor line_end is given. So get_dayz_file('P:\DZ\sounds\hpp\config.cpp', line_start=1) returned 10,239,845 characters (523,051 lines), and the size error only appeared when no range was passed. An agent that passes just a start line on a big config.cpp or mapgroupcluster.xml gets megabytes back and floods its context. A second, latent mismatch: _slice_lines uses str.splitlines(), but the indexer's _split_lines deliberately splits on '\n' only, because splitlines also breaks at \f, \v, \x1c-\x1e, \x85 and \u2028. For 'a\fb\nc', the server returns 'b' as line 2 where the indexer counts 'c'. A scan of P:\scripts and P:\DZ found no such characters today, so this only bites on future or modded files. Minor issues: _read_manifest does not catch UnicodeDecodeError, so a manifest that is not valid UTF-8 errors without the rebuild hint. The search docstring lists stale_reason as always present, but it only appears on stale hits.

Almost everything checks out. All 36 scripts\dayz rows, the 6 setup rows and the 3 dev rows match a real .bat file, and every wrapper's target script exists. Every flag or subcommand used in an example is in the target's --help: --author, --source, --piece, vest, gate build, --stdin, --server, --mod, check, --merge, --version, --mission, --full, --grep, --keep-server, --remove, --status, --agents. The Python fallback note is accurate: stop-test.bat has no fallback, and dayz-search.bat is the only scripts\dayz wrapper without the [FAIL] line. The paid-API notes are accurate: Voyage, the free-tier prompt in index.py, TypeSafe Jev only when the key is set, and evals.bat costing tokens. The panel install line matches .claude-plugin/marketplace.json. The clean-repo and clean-workspace rows match their code: .git folders are skipped, and --include-server removes all of .server. Its tests in scripts/dev/test_repo_integrity.py pass. The full run (py -m pytest -q .claude scripts/dev hooks) gave 3 failed and 4525 passed; none of the 3 failures involves this README. Problems a user would hit: (1) The sync-skills.bat row says 'Claude Code with --agents claude'. Running `sync-skills.bat --agents claude` links only Claude Code and drops Codex and Gemini, because --agents replaces the default list in sync.py. A user who wants all three gets one. (2) The clean-workspace.bat row says it deletes the deployed P:\Mods\@<ModName>\ copies. clean.py removes one only when its ownership marker matches, so a hand-copied or older deploy stays and the user does not know why. (3) The Python-missing message only covers scripts\dayz. The setup wrappers, which a new user runs first (for example preflight.bat), have no [FAIL] guard. Without Python the user gets a bare 'py is not recognized' error, and the README says nothing about that case. (4) The ask.bat note says every question goes to Voyage. Without VOYAGE_API_KEY, ask.py falls back to grep on its own, which the README does not say.

All 49 tests in hooks/test_scope_guard.py pass (8.8 seconds), and every test drives the hook through stdin. The output is correct PreToolUse JSON: hookSpecificOutput holds hookEventName PreToolUse, permissionDecision deny and a reason Claude can act on. Bad stdin, a corrupt state file and errors inside the hook all exit 0 with no output, so the hook never blocks on its own bug. The project wiring in .claude/settings.json and the plugin wiring in hooks/hooks.json both match Edit|Write|MultiEdit and have a 10-second timeout. The docstring matches the code. I also probed paths by hand. These were blocked: short 8.3 names (OTHERM~1, WORKSP~1, including a file that does not exist yet), alternate data streams (a.c:ads), the ::$INDEX_ALLOCATION directory form, non-ASCII file names, and the P:\Other and P:\Mods\@Other forms. Two gaps remain that a user would actually hit. First, a sibling mod that is still being created is not guarded: while scoped to MyVest, Claude can write workspace/BrandNew/scripts/3_Game/x.c, mod.cpp and the rest of a new mod, as long as config.cpp or $PBOPREFIX$ is written last. Only the marker write at the folder root is caught. Second, the hook matches Edit, Write and MultiEdit only, so a Bash or PowerShell write into another mod's folder (redirect, cp, sed -i, Set-Content) passes. The docstring states this second gap. There are also small test gaps: no test covers the 8.3 short-name claim, a state file whose JSON is valid but not an object, or a missing preflight.py or game install on the !Workshop path.

All 18 tests pass in 0.16s, and the full suite (1417 tests) passes. Each scan has a test that feeds it a synthetic bad case, so the checks for modded-member clashes, cross-file names and layers, duplicate RPC handlers and unused fields are each shown to fail when they should. Every P: citation holds when opened: staminahandler.c:335-338 sets stamina from GetStaminaMax, cfggameplayhandler.c:217-220 is GetStaminaMax, playerbase.c:4607-4610 is the EOnFrame client and IsControlledPlayer guard, dayzgame.c:2848 and :2914-2917 forward OnKeyPress to the mission, and uimanager.c:59 is GetMenu. Three concrete defects remain. First, _method_body counts braces in the raw source without removing strings or comments, so a method that later gains a line such as Print("}") or a comment ending in '}' is cut short. The hover, hotkey, stamina and EOnFrame tests then fail even though the code is correct, or pass without having looked at it. Second, _cross_file_problems searches code that still contains string literals, so a Print("MyMod_Item") in another file counts as a use and wrongly demands a note naming the declaring file. Third, the _FUNC negative lookahead skips any line that starts with 'static', so two files that each declare the same file-scope static function would not be reported as a duplicate.

I opened every P: citation in the file (canteen.c:1, playerbase.c:359-364, 2042, 3007, 3129, 6170, 6733, 8121, 7353-7361, 7408-7421, entityai.c:227, 2843-2850, 3064, eagents.c:9, poisoning.c:32, staminahandler.c:335-338 and 1081, cfggameplayhandler.c:217-220, cfggameplaydatajson.c:135, constants.c:749, playerstatspco.c:340, playerconstants.c:45, missionserver.c:781, missiongameplay.c:230, inventory.c:121-128, gameplay.c:4-11, presethandlers.c:179, bloodregen.c:14, and characters config.cpp:122, 378-382, 412-414). Two concrete defects remain. (1) The IS_EXHAUSTED check in MyMod_UpdateSyncFlags (line 98) compares raw stamina against 10. The same file explains that raw stamina runs from 0 to the server's staminaMax setting and adds MyMod_GetStaminaPct for that reason, but this check does not use it. On a server with staminaMax set to 1000, the flag only turns on at 1 percent stamina. (2) OnScheduledTick (lines 140-150) does its work after super returns. Vanilla's early return for players who are not selected or not alive (playerbase.c:3009-3010) only exits the super call, so the mod still decays reputation and rebuilds sync flags for dead and not-yet-selected players. Two smaller points: the null check in MyMod_GetStaminaPct (line 243) can never fire, because vanilla Init creates the stamina handler (playerbase.c:414). OnStoreLoad also does not reject a save whose version is newer than MYMOD_PLAYER_STORE_VERSION, which happens after a mod downgrade.

Line 52 says that to copy autokey on purpose you call bpy_extras.anim_utils.AutoKeying.key_transformation(context, target). In bpy_extras.anim_utils, key_transformation takes (target, options) and keys without checking the user's autokey setting. The method that follows autokey is autokey_transformation(context, target). A script written from line 52 would pass the wrong arguments or key the wrong thing. To reach A+, change line 52 to name AutoKeying.autokey_transformation(context, target), or describe key_transformation(target, options) correctly.

It sets parent.location = (5, 5, 5) through the data API and then reads parent.matrix_world.inverted() on the next line, claiming the child goes back to (1, 0, 0). A bare transform write does not update matrix_world until the depsgraph is evaluated, so the inverse comes out as identity and the child stays at (6, 5, 5). To reach A+, add bpy.context.view_layer.update() in that snippet after parent.location is set and before matrix_parent_inverse is assigned (lines 89 to 92).
